[Alder Creek Reference Facts]
Type: Knowledge
Source: Fictional Reference Archive
Process Every: 5

Fact 01 — Alder Creek Observatory.
The fictional Alder Creek Observatory opened in 1987 on North Ridge.

Fact 02 — Clock tower.
The town clock tower has four faces and was restored in 2011.

Fact 03 — River.
The Silverbrook River flows east through Alder Creek.

Fact 04 — Library.
The Alder Creek Public Library occupies a former railway depot.

Fact 05 — Bridge.
The covered Maple Bridge was rebuilt after a flood in 1996.

Fact 06 — Museum.
The town museum preserves a 1932 printing press.

Fact 07 — Festival.
Lantern Night takes place on the first Saturday in November.

Fact 08 — Transit.
Route 7 connects the library, hospital, and train station.

Fact 09 — Weather station.
Station AC-04 records rainfall at North Ridge.

Fact 10 — Botanical garden.
The garden contains a greenhouse called the Glass House.

Fact 11 — Founders.
Mara Vale and Owen Reed founded Alder Creek in 1894.

Fact 12 — School.
Alder Creek High School's mascot is the heron.

Fact 13 — Local paper.
The Alder Creek Ledger publishes on Thursdays.

Fact 14 — Cafe.
The Blue Finch Cafe opened in 2008.

Fact 15 — Trail.
The Cedar Loop trail is 4.2 kilometers long.

Fact 16 — Archive.
Museum box B-17 holds the 1948 flood photographs.

Fact 17 — Radio.
Community station KACR broadcasts on 91.3 FM in the fictional setting.

Fact 18 — Theater.
The Oriole Theater has 240 seats.

Fact 19 — Map.
The fictional town map divides Alder Creek into five districts.

Fact 20 — Test code.
The archive access phrase for this fictional exercise is SILVER HERON 42.
